title: Training Dataset Matters for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials: Water Simulation as an Example
abstract:
arXiv:2512.23939v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Accurate predictions of machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) rely on training datasets covering relevant thermodynamic conditions and phases. Using water as an example, we show that insufficiently sampled datasets of MLIPs lead to wrong predictions of densities, melting temperatures, and nuclear quantum effects. In contrast, MLIPs trained on comprehensive datasets with the same electronic structure method yield consistent property predictions agnostic of MLIP architecture, with densities in quantitative agreement with reference calculations.
relevance_reason: Key author: Roberto Car

title: Electrified Metal-Water Interfaces at Constant Potential: Data-Efficient Transfer Learning for Machine-Learning-Based Molecular Dynamics
abstract:
arXiv:2511.19338v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Simulating electrified metal-water interfaces with explicit solvent under constant potential is essential for understanding electrochemical processes, yet remains prohibitively expensive with ab initio methods. We present TRECI, a data-efficient workflow for constructing machine learning force-fields (ML-FFs) that achieve ab initio-level accuracy in electronically grand-canonical molecular dynamics. By leveraging transfer learning from general-purpose and domain-specific models, TRECI enables stable and accurate simulations across a wide potential range using a reduced number of reference configurations. This efficiency allows the use of high-level meta-GGA functionals and rigorous surface-electrification schemes. Applied to Cu(111)-water, models trained on just one thousand configurations yield accurate molecular dynamics simulations, capturing bias-dependent solvent restructuring effects not previously reported. TRECI offers a general strategy for characterising diverse materials and interfacial chemistries, significantly lowering the cost of realistic constant-potential simulations and expanding access to quantitative electrochemical modelling.
relevance_reason: Key author: Michele Parrinello

title: Rethinking Negative Prompting for Concept Suppression: Unconditional Anchoring and Localized Guidance
abstract:
arXiv:2412.07658v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Text-to-image diffusion models have rapidly transitioned from research prototypes to widely deployed tools. Along with their impressive capabilities, these models can also generate harmful or undesirable content (e.g., NSFW imagery), motivating practical mechanisms for removing such concepts. Negative prompting, which uses the negative-prompt prediction as the guidance anchor, is among the most widely used mechanisms for steering sampling trajectories away from unwanted concepts. However, for jailbreak prompts, it can fail in a regime we refer to as \emph{guidance collapse}, where the model's denoising predictions for the prompt and negative prompt become similar, so that the guidance difference driving negative prompting vanishes and the guided prediction degenerates to the negative-prompt prediction, undermining suppression. To fix this issue, we propose TraSCE (Trajectory Steering for ConcEpt Suppression), a training-free inference-time method that makes negative prompting reliable under guidance collapse. TraSCE combines two complementary components: (i) unconditional anchoring, which makes the fallback under guidance collapse a neutral unconditional prediction rather than the negative-prompt prediction, and (ii) an alignment-localized steering step, which deliberately induces this collapse for adversarial prompts and steers the sample to the unconditional fallback, while remaining minimally intrusive on benign prompts. We evaluate TraSCE on adversarial prompt benchmarks targeting nudity and violence, and further demonstrate its applicability to suppressing artistic styles and objects. Across these settings, TraSCE substantially improves the robustness of negative prompting to jailbreak prompts without any training, weight updates, or pre-collected concept-specific data (prompts or images), while keeping the impact on general image quality small.
relevance_reason: Key author: Anubhav Jain

title: pymatgen: 15 years of community growth, new functionality, and future prospects
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23538v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a retrospective on the Python Materials Genomics (pymatgen) library, reflecting on 15 years of community growth and established best practices. The current version of pymatgen builds on its robust, open-source foundation, emphasising its collaborative nature. Over the past decade, pymatgen has thrived as one of the largest open-source materials science codebases. We detail how pymatgen supports advanced computational materials science workflows, how it adapts to changing demands, and the lessons learned from its growing community, providing guidance beyond pymatgen's open-source community. Pymatgen will continue to evolve in response to the current rapidly changing landscape of computational materials science and materials informatics. We discuss the challenges and potential solutions to managing the community-driven evolution of pymatgen and provide an outlook on its future development.
relevance_reason: Key author: Tess E. Smidt, Kristin A. Persson, Anubhav Jain, Shyue Ping Ong

title: Scalable long-range machine learning interatomic potentials with electrical response for atomistic material modeling
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23643v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate atomistic simulations of materials under electric fields require long-range electrostatics and electrical-response modeling at length scales beyond the reach of conventional first-principles methods. Yet these capabilities remain difficult to reconcile with the scalability of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Strictly local models enable efficient spatial parallelization but neglect long-range interactions, whereas existing electrostatic extensions introduce global dependencies that hinder distributed computation. Here, we overcome this limitation by analytically separating the long-range electrostatic forces and Born effective charges (BECs) into a global electrostatics calculation and strictly local derivatives of learned latent charges. This formulation preserves the spatial decomposability of equivariant MLIPs while enabling distributed evaluation of energies, forces, stresses, and BECs across different boundary conditions. Implemented as DPA4C-LR on the \texttt{nvalchemi} platform, the framework scales to 5.2 million atoms on four GPUs at approximately twice the computational cost of its short-range backbone. Trained on energies and forces, DPA4C-LR accurately infers BECs and reproduces the field-dependent infrared spectra of water. We further demonstrate its capabilities by recovering the characteristic slim polarization hysteresis of relaxor \ce{Pb(Mg_{1/3}Nb_{2/3})O3}, which is obscured by finite-size effects in smaller simulations; predicting a room-temperature field-driven ionic conductivity of $6.8 \pm 0.7$~mS/cm in amorphous \ce{Li_{0.9}NbO_{0.9}Cl_{4.1}}; and modeling interfacial thermal transport across Si/diamond interfaces with slab-corrected electrostatics. By combining long-range physics, electrical-response inference, and distributed computation, this framework extends predictive atomistic modeling toward device-relevant length scales.
relevance_reason: Develops a scalable long-range equivariant machine-learned interatomic potential with analytical Born effective charges (DPA4C-LR) evaluated on millions of atoms, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP development and large-scale MD-type evaluation, and (c) advances atomistic simulation under electric fields.

title: Foundation-Model Supervision of Distilled Potentials for Million-Atom Molecular Dynamics
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials distilled from foundation models enable fast large-scale molecular dynamics (MD), but they can fail locally in chemical environments that their training data did not sample. System-averaged error metrics and small random audits often miss such sparse or isolated failures. Here we use an exact equivariant foundation model, MACE-MPA-0, to check every atom of million-atom production simulations. Reorganizing two-layer MACE inference into a receiver-chunked three-pass schedule that keeps no per-edge intermediates resident reduces the marginal memory per atom 340-fold, evaluates up to $2.86\times10^{7}$ atoms on a single H200 GPU, and supervises $10^{6}$-atom trajectories in LAMMPS at 1.3% of the run time. Distilled MACE students run four to nine times slower than NEP89 with 0.95-1.28 times the teacher's force error against density functional theory (DFT). In molten SiO$_2$, whole-system checks uncover a persistent tail of under-coordinated atoms hidden by the system-averaged error and an isolated, unphysical O-O contact that a 1% random audit misses 94% of the time. On-the-fly retraining on teacher-labelled 13-{\AA} clusters, with the force loss restricted to their inner 6 {\AA}, removes three quarters of the failure tail and the kilobar-level pressure biases in SiO$_2$ and compressed water; the repair converges to the teacher, not to DFT.
relevance_reason: Uses a MACE foundation MLIP to supervise/repair distilled potentials and runs million-atom LAMMPS MD of SiO2 and water, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP development/benchmarking plus MD, and (c) advancing MLIP distillation and validation methodology.

title: AceFF: A State-of-the-Art Machine Learning Potential for Small Molecules
abstract:
arXiv:2601.00581v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We introduce AceFF, a pre-trained machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) optimized for small molecule drug discovery. While MLIPs have emerged as efficient alternatives to Density Functional Theory (DFT), generalizability across diverse chemical spaces remains difficult. AceFF addresses this by refining the TensorNet2 architecture and training it on a comprehensive dataset of drug-like compounds. This approach yields a force field that balances high-throughput inference speed with DFT-level accuracy. We introduce two models sharing the same architecture: \mbox{AceFF-2}, trained on our own dataset of small molecules and supporting the essential medicinal chemistry elements (H, B, C, N, O, F, Si, P, S, Cl, Br, I); and \mbox{AceFF-2-OMOL}, trained on a subset of OMol25 containing the AceFF-2 elements plus the common biomolecular ion elements Na and K. The models are explicitly trained to handle charged states. Validation against rigorous benchmarks, including complex torsional energy scans, molecular dynamics trajectories, batched minimizations, and tests of force and energy accuracy, demonstrates that AceFF is state-of-the-art for organic molecules in the accuracy and speed regime important for drug discovery. The AceFF-2 and AceFF-2-OMol model weights and inference code are available at https://huggingface.co/Acellera/AceFF-2.0 and https://huggingface.co/Acellera/AceFF-2-OMOL.
relevance_reason: Introduces AceFF, a pre-trained MLIP (TensorNet2-based) trained on drug-like molecules and validated on torsional scans, MD trajectories, and force/energy accuracy, cleanly satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP development/training, and (c) benchmarking.

title: Multitask learning with semiempirical orbital charges enables sample-efficient MLIPs
abstract:
arXiv:2605.24073v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) require generating computationally expensive, large-scale training datasets to accurately simulate materials and molecules. Incorporating electronic structure information using multitask learning improves sample efficiency, however, training on full Hamiltonian matrices, which scale quadratically with the number of atoms, is intractable for large datasets. In this work, we show that multitask learning utilizing orbitally resolved semiempirical charges significantly improves sample efficiency and accuracy in MLIPs. To efficiently predict orbital charges, we implement a specialized equivariant model, reducing charge prediction error compared to an invariant baseline. By augmenting training with computationally inexpensive GFN1-xTB orbital charges, which scale linearly with the number of atoms, our model achieves a 58% reduction in energy mean absolute error relative to energy-only baselines, and requires five times less data to match their performance. Against the stronger baseline of joint energy-and-force training, orbital charges still reduce the energy error by 12%. Furthermore, our approach matches or outperforms models trained on expensive density functional theory (DFT) atomic charges, capturing orbitally resolved electronic complexity and forcing the network to learn a physically accurate latent space that spontaneously clusters metals by shared chemical properties. Because orbital charges are only required during training, this approach preserves inference efficiency, providing a scalable recipe for developing accurate, data-efficient foundation models for complex chemical systems.
relevance_reason: Multitask MLIP training augmented with GFN1-xTB orbital charges, with explicit-atom energy/force learning and sample-efficiency benchmarks, satisfying (a) atoms, (b) MLIP development, and (c) method advance.

title: Linear response for machine-learned interatomic potentials: phonons at arbitrary wave vectors from the primitive cell
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23545v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Phonon calculations with machine-learned interatomic potentials are almost exclusively performed with finite displacements in supercells, an approach that is exact only at wave vectors commensurate with the supercell and whose error depends on the range of the force constants. In message-passing networks this range grows with the number of layers, and reaches 140 angstrom for the deepest universal models. Here we show that the dynamical matrix of a message-passing potential can be obtained exactly in the primitive cell, at any wave vector, as the linear response of the forces to a displacement modulated by a Bloch phase, in the spirit of density-functional perturbation theory. The phase enters only where the features of neighboring atoms are gathered, and the trained model is used without modification. One further derivative yields group velocities and mode Gr\"uneisen parameters analytically. We apply the method to NequIP and Prophet, and reproduce the Hessians of supercells to machine precision. Using these results as a reference, we find that the supercells commonly employed in high-throughput calculations lead to errors of several tenths of a THz in the phonon frequencies, and that these errors decrease slowly with the size of the supercell, in particular for deep models. For a low-symmetry silicate, the supercell predicts a dynamical instability that the model does not have. Quantities that depend on derivatives of the dispersion, such as the group velocities and the Gr\"uneisen parameter at low temperature, are considerably more affected than the frequencies themselves. When both approaches are used to obtain the same force constants, their computational cost is comparable for crystals with symmetry.
relevance_reason: Derives exact linear-response dynamical matrices for message-passing machine-learned interatomic potentials (NequIP, Prophet) at arbitrary wave vectors, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP development/benchmarking, and (c) a methodological advance for phonon calculations.

title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23776v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Developing a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) that is accurate for the specific conditions under which it will be applied, rather than simply for the predefined configurations chosen by the model developer, is a significant challenge in atomistic simulation. Active learning (AL) addresses this challenge by closing the loop between candidate generation, data selection, reference calculation, and model updating. Here, we survey more than seventy studies, with an emphasis on work from 2020 to 2026, to understand how active learning has evolved from a niche, on-the-fly training technique for query-by-committee and Gaussian process force fields into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies. he reviewed examples include on-the-fly molecular dynamics, active data selection for fine-tuning pretrained models, kernel- and representation-based acquisition using frozen pretrained models, and reaction-aware sampling for chemical systems far from equilibrium. We explore the use of active learning in elemental and alloy mechanics, hydrogen and ion diffusion, ferroelectrics and effective Hamiltonians of functional materials, reactive and photochemical dynamics, high-entropy and compositionally disordered materials, as well as generative and autonomous material discovery pipelines. Drawing on a growing body of critical, methodologically self-aware literature, we also show that this achievement carries systematic caveats. Uncertainty estimates are not interchangeable across model architectures and are frequently the least reliable exactly where they matter most. We close by discussing the outlook for standardized, uncertainty-calibrated, and observable-targeted active-learning workflows in the foundation-model era.
relevance_reason: Review of active learning strategies for training machine-learned interatomic potentials (query-by-committee, on-the-fly MD, fine-tuning), directly addressing MLIP development and training-data methodology, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: From Surface Reactions to Inhibitor Coverage: A Machine-Learning-Assisted Computational Study of Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22911v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) enables selective material growth for the fabrication of nanoscale semiconductor devices. Predicting inhibitor coverage is essential for understanding and optimizing surface blocking in AS-ALD. Here, we present a computational workflow combining a pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potential with off-lattice grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations and apply it to inhibitor adsorption and precursor blocking on amorphous SiO2. Realistic surface models reveal substantial site-dependent variations in reaction energies and activation barriers, with silanol groups serving as the primary adsorption sites for aminosilane and related inhibitors and metal precursors. Coverage simulations show that inhibitors producing identical adsorbed fragments can yield different coverages because the intact molecules impose distinct steric constraints, leading to different accessible site densities and blocking capabilities. Beyond coverage, we highlight the importance of the reactivity of adsorbed inhibitor fragments toward precursors in determining inhibitor stability and blocking performance. Together, these findings demonstrate the need to consider both steric effects and chemical reactivity on realistic amorphous surfaces. Our calculations connect local reaction chemistry with inhibitor coverage and provide a computational basis for understanding inhibition mechanisms and selecting suitable inhibitor-precursor combinations for AS-ALD.
relevance_reason: Uses a pretrained universal machine-learned interatomic potential with off-lattice grand canonical Monte Carlo on realistic amorphous SiO2 surfaces, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP plus MC, and (c) an application to inhibitor coverage in area-selective ALD.

title: Thermal Conductivity and Temperature-Induced Band Gap Renormalization in Crystalline and Amorphous Ga$_2$O$_3$
abstract:
arXiv:2603.29484v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) and electron-phonon interactions in crystalline and amorphous gallium oxide are herein determined by coupling a machine-learned interatomic potential, namely the moment tensor potential (MTP) model, to first-principles calculations. Crystalline $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ exhibits a substantial band gap renormalization (BGR) of $\sim$0.45 eV at 700 K, with $\sim$0.2 eV caused by zero-point BGR. The computed temperature dependence of BGR induced by classical nuclear motion in $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ is stronger than that in amorphous Ga$_2$O$_3$, with the difference in BGR reaching $\sim$0.18 eV at 900 K. Thermal transport calculations reveal that the LTC of amorphous Ga$_2$O$_3$ remains near $0.9$ W$\cdot$ m$^{-1}$$\cdot$K$^{-1}$ for temperatures between 300 K and 700 K, which is approximately an order of magnitude lower than that of crystalline $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$. Overall, the presented framework provides a computationally tractable and reliable route for predicting properties of semiconductors (both crystalline and amorphous) under operating conditions relevant to microelectronics and optoelectronics.
relevance_reason: Moment tensor potential MLIP coupled with first-principles calculations to run atomistic simulations of thermal conductivity and band-gap renormalization, cleanly satisfying (a)-(c) via MLIP-driven simulation.

title: Lattice thermal conductivity of Ti<sub>3</sub>C<sub>2</sub> MXene via deep-learning potential
abstract:
Publication date: January 2027
Source: Computational Materials Science, Volume 276
Author(s): Zexiang Deng

title: Electrochemical Molecular Dynamics within the Finite-Field Framework
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23291v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Electrochemical processes at charged interfaces lie at the heart of modern technologies and their continued improvement depends on insights into the relevant atomistic processes. However, the necessary tools to impose constant-voltage conditions in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations typically directly target the electrode charge, making their extension to methods that go beyond an empirical description of metals more cumbersome. In this work, we propose an MD protocol to realize a thermodynamic ensemble in which voltage control is attained, but which is formulated purely within the framework of finite-field simulations in 3D periodic boundary conditions. We show a derivation and implementation of such a control device, which we coin an electrostat, in the ELECTRODE package within LAMMPS. Our simulations systematically benchmark the derived theory against other established approaches, for example, showing its equivalence to a potentiostat, and quantify the importance of properly accounting for ensemble fluctuations. We find that for systems of several thousands of atoms, one obtains the same equilibrium properties with the electrostat as with a simpler constant-field simulation. The difference between the two methods only manifests itself at smaller length scales, thereby establishing practical limits for the inclusion of voltage fluctuations in atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems. The strength of this framework also lies in its simplicity of extension to first-principles ab initio and reactive machine-learning potentials.
relevance_reason: Derives and implements an 'electrostat' constant-voltage MD protocol in LAMMPS with explicit-atom electrochemical simulations and benchmarks against potentiostat/constant-field approaches, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MD method development, and (c) advancing simulation methodology.

title: The effect of oxygen on the surface tension of AlTi metallic alloys
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23286v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We perform molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of AlTi metallic alloy melts, with a specific focus on surface properties and the effect of oxygen. The simulations use a machine-learned inter- action potential (MLIP) that has recently been tested through experimental data for the statical and dynamical properties of AlTi melts in the bulk [Kato et al. (2026)]. We find that the surface- tension response to oxygen depends strongly on the AlTi composition. Element-resolved density profiles show that oxygen enrichment near the interface is accompanied by a suppression of the Al surface segregation observed in the oxygen-free liquid. The results are compared to experimental values obtained using levitation techniques in microgravity.
relevance_reason: Molecular dynamics simulations of AlTi alloy melts with a machine-learned interatomic potential to compute surface tension and oxygen segregation, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP-driven MD, and (c) an application to interfacial properties validated against experiment.

title: Towards decoding the structure of water-magnetite interface
abstract:
arXiv:2410.12717v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The molecular structure of water at iron-oxide interfaces is determined by the protonation state, orientation and population of interfacial OH species. These microscopic features can be decoded by combining surface-specific vibrational spectroscopy with reactive and accurate molecular dynamics simulations. In this way, it could be possible to connect the measured nonlinear optical response to specific molecular configurations at the magnetite-water interface, resolving the interfacial water structure. We investigated magnetite films in contact with liquid water at neutral and alkaline pH using phase-resolved sum-frequency generation (SFG) spectroscopy in the OH/OD stretching region and Fresnel correction of the optical response. In parallel, neural-network-potential molecular dynamics simulations were used to model the water-magnetite interface and identify interfacial water species, quantify their orientations, hydrogen-bonding environments and lifetimes, and compute species resolved SFG spectra. The combined analysis assigns distinct spectral features to dissociated surface OH groups, hydroxyls and water molecules adsorbed on octahedral iron sites, water bound at dissociation sites and water molecules above tetrahedral rows. The simulations reveal a reactive interfacial hydroxyl network with nanosecond-scale rearrangements and strong species-dependent hydrogen bonding. Experimentally, the SFG spectra show pronounced pH dependence, consistent with changes in surface charge and hydroxylation. A systematic difference between measured and computed SFG spectra indicates that the assumed surface model of magnetite does not fully represent the aqueous interface. This discrepancy provides a molecular constraint for improved models of magnetite-water interfaces and highlights SFG spectroscopy/ML-MD comparison as a valuable route to resolving oxide-water interfacial structures.
relevance_reason: Combines neural-network-potential MD of the water-magnetite interface with computed species-resolved SFG spectra, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP-driven MD, and (c) interfacial structure/dynamics application.

title: Interplay between high-entropy effects and the superionic transition in fluorite oxides: A liquid-like perspective
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22850v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Minor actinide (MA)-bearing mixed oxide (MOX), a prominent high-entropy ceramic (HEC), is a promising candidate for advanced fast reactor fuels. Using a hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics (MC/MD) approach, we reveal that Np and Am segregation establishes a distinct short-range order (SRO) that induces severe lattice distortion. We uncover a competitive mechanism between localized high-entropy blocking effects and collective superionic dynamics, where the anionic kinetic and structural evolution within the 2000-2800 K range is partitioned and governed by the Tammann crossover temperature and superionic transition temperature. In the low-temperature regime, severe lattice distortions induced by the SRO structures create localized electrostatic and strain-coupled potential wells, which spatially confine the O-ions and lead to their sluggish diffusion. The system exhibits increased dynamical heterogeneity as thermal activation alleviates these structural constraints. Crucially, these localized traps spontaneously transform into a highly interconnected, string-like polyhedral topological network. Driven by the maximization of configurational entropy, this structural change creates low-viscosity transport pathways that trigger confinement-enhanced diffusion. Consequently, a dramatic kinetic inversion occurs, where the O-ion mobility of SRO model surpasses that of random solid solution (RSS) model via an entropy-driven compensation mechanism. Finally, through Gibbs free energy minimization and defect analysis, structural and thermodynamic origins of the superionic transition in HEC are elucidated. This study unveils how local chemical ordering regulates ion transport under extreme conditions, providing theoretical support for the design of high-performance nuclear fuels with both superior radiation tolerance and optimized mass transfer capabilities.
relevance_reason: Hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulations of explicit-atom fluorite oxide solid solutions reveal short-range order and superionic O-ion transport, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MC/MD methodology, and (c) an application advancing understanding of high-entropy oxide transport.

title: Synergistic Self-Driven Nanoconfinement and Dynamical Heterogeneity in Deeply Supercooled "No Man's Land" Water
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22402v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: The 150--235 K ``no man's land'' (NML) of deeply supercooled water is a highly debated regime where rapid crystallization hinders experimental observation of the hypothesized liquid-liquid phase transition. Using TIP4P/2005 molecular dynamics simulations, we uncover a structurally and dynamically heterogeneous state at ambient pressure that exhibits novel physical features. Our results demonstrate that this low-density state ($\rho \approx 0.925$ g/cm$^3$) is a unique supercooled liquid, distinct from both glassy and spinodal states. Specifically, it emerges as a stable, structurally arrested phase driven by a self-generated ``soft skeleton'' of nanoclusters. This network forms an intrinsic nanoporous structure that imposes nanoconfinement on the remaining fluid, proving that NML confinement can be an entirely self-driven phenomenon. Finally, we resolve the temperature-dependent, nonlinear behavior of density and compressibility, highlighting a structurally driven anomaly that clarifies the thermodynamics of deep supercooling. Collectively, this work provides a transformative structural framework for understanding the anomalous nature of water within the NML.
relevance_reason: Classical molecular dynamics with the TIP4P/2005 water force field investigating deeply supercooled water structure and dynamics, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) classical MD, and (c) application to a physical system.

title: Pressure-Dependent hcp-to-fcc Phase Transition Path Derived from Exact Lattice Summations over Inverse Power Law Potentials
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22855v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate the phase transition between hexagonal close-packed (hcp) and face-centered cubic (fcc) structures along the Burgers-Bain transformation path at pressures up to several hundred gigapascals. We consider a hierarchy of interatomic potentials, from $(n,m)$-Lennard-Jones potentials to extended Lennard-Jones two-body interactions in terms of inverse-power expansions and the Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body term, alongside density functional theory (DFT) calculations for solid argon. For inverse-power potentials, free energies are evaluated through exact lattice sums and efficient integral representations based on generalizations of the Epstein zeta function to anisotropic interaction kernels, followed by lattice-parameter optimization. This methodology enables an accurate determination of the pressure-dependent Burgers-Bain minimum-energy path and the associated activation barrier for the phase transition. The transformation exhibits pronounced symmetry breaking connecting the Burgers and Bain paths, a feature confirmed by DFT calculations. At high pressure, the hcp-to-fcc activation barrier increases approximately linearly with pressure, owing to the dominant pressure-volume contribution. Including entropy and anharmonic effects yields excellent agreement with experimental temperature-dependent volumes up to the melting point. DFT results also highlight the increasing importance of many-body interactions under compression. Whereas two-body potentials predict that the path passes through the body-centered cubic (bcc) structure only at very high pressures, DFT generally predicts a pathway that bypasses bcc. The Axilrod-Teller-Muto term slightly reduces this discrepancy. Furthermore, DFT performs better at high pressures, where dispersion forces become less important.
relevance_reason: Computes hcp-to-fcc transition paths via classical interatomic potentials (Lennard-Jones, Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body) with exact lattice sums plus DFT for solid argon, involving lattice-parameter optimization and barrier evaluation, so (a) explicit atoms, (b) classical force fields/DFT and geometry optimization, and (c) method advance are all satisfied.

title: No source-free exchange-correlation magnetic fields in non-collinear spin-density functional theory
abstract:
arXiv:2609.01533v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The source-free condition, $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{xc}}=0$, where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{xc}}=\delta E_{\mathrm{xc}}/\delta\mathbf{m}$ is the exchange-correlation (xc) magnetic field of non-collinear spin-density functional theory (SDFT) and $\mathbf{m}$ the magnetization, is widely believed to be exact. Recent studies report that projecting the field of a parent functional onto its source-free part improves the predicted magnetic moments. We show that the condition violates the global spin-rotation symmetry of $E_{\mathrm{xc}}$ and therefore cannot be exact. A source-free field is exact only in a transverse theory whose xc functional differs from $E_{\mathrm{xc}}$ and is itself not invariant under spin rotations. We examine a source-free (SoF) construction, an exchange-correlation energy given by a parent SDFT functional evaluated at the transverse magnetization $\mathbf{m}_{\perp}$. Its field is divergence-free, remains a functional derivative and exerts local torques, but still, it breaks global spin-rotation symmetry. With the LSDA as parent we examine the \ce{Mn2} molecule. The SoF and the locally collinear (LoC) LSDA both give too short a bond and too large a bond energy, but SoF finds a broken-symmetry antiferromagnetic solution, consistent with the experimentally observed $^{1}\Sigma^{+}_{g}$ ground state, with a coupling of the right sign and roughly the right size, while LoC finds a high-spin $^{11}\Pi_{u}$ ferromagnet and the wrong sign. The broken symmetry of SoF, however, produces severe errors in directional properties: a rigid spin rotation of the magnetization changes the energy by about $1\,\mathrm{eV}$, in a weak uniform field the magnetization points perpendicular to the field instead of antiparallel to it, and the molecule develops a spurious magnetic anisotropy.
relevance_reason: Develops and tests a new non-collinear spin-DFT exchange-correlation functional construction (source-free field, transverse magnetization) with explicit-atom application to the Mn2 molecule's bond length/energy and magnetic ordering, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT, and (c) method advance.
